conversation.text: A block of mass 2kg is placed on a rough surface. Find the torque about the pivot if F = 10N at r = 0.5m.

conversation.gapDescription: Before torque, recall Newton's 2nd Law: net force equals mass times acceleration, F = ma. Torque extends this rotational idea — it measures how a force tends to rotate a body about a pivot rather than translate it.
steps: Torque is defined as the product of the force and the perpendicular distance from the pivot.
Substituting the given values with the force perpendicular to the lever arm (θ = 90°): $$\tau = 0.5\text{ m} \times 10\text{ N} = 5\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
The torque about the pivot is $5\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$, directed such that it tends to rotate the block about the pivot point.
conversation.keyInsight: The mass (2kg) is a distractor here — torque depends only on force and lever arm, not on the object's weight unless gravity itself provides the force.

diagnosticQuiz.questionText: A force of F = 20N is applied at a distance r = 0.4m from the pivot. What is the torque if the force is perpendicular to the moment arm?
diagnosticQuiz.hint: Check your multiplication — torque = r × F = 0.4 × 20

weakPoint.title: Sign Convention in Torque
weakPoint.description: You correctly applied τ = r × F but missed how the direction of rotation affects the sign. Revisit the right-hand rule and clockwise vs counter-clockwise conventions.

questions.text: A uniform rod of length L and mass M is pivoted at one end. A horizontal force F is applied at the free end. Find the angular acceleration of the rod.
solution: The torque about the pivot due to force F at the free end equals $\tau = F \cdot L$.
Moment of inertia of a uniform rod about one end is $I = \frac{1}{3}ML^2$.
Applying $\tau = I\alpha$ and solving for $\alpha$ gives the angular acceleration: $$\alpha = \frac{\tau}{I} = \frac{F \cdot L}{\frac{1}{3}ML^2} = \frac{3F}{2ML}$$
questions.keyInsight: Always use the moment of inertia about the actual axis of rotation — here the pivot, not the center of mass. Mixing up axes is the most common error in rotational dynamics.

questions.text: A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls without slipping down an inclined plane of angle θ. Find the acceleration of the cylinder.
solution: For rolling without slipping down an incline, acceleration is given by $a = \frac{g \sin\theta}{1 + \frac{I}{MR^2}}$.
The moment of inertia of a solid cylinder is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$.
questions.keyInsight: Rolling motion combines translational and rotational motion. The friction force acts backwards to produce torque, but does no work since the point of contact is instantaneously at rest.
